source.title: Learning One-hidden-layer ReLU Networks via Gradient Descent
source.authors: Xiao Zhang; Yaodong Yu; Ling-Xiao Wang; Quanquan Gu

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no obvious truncation or garbling affecting the relevant sections.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports gradient-descent experiments and analysis bearing on learning shallow ReLU networks, but uses synthetic teacher-generated data and parameter recovery rather than benchmark classification error.
record.gate_note: Reports synthetic experiments on convergence, sample complexity and estimation error. The initialization comparison is a reported outcome; cited results from prior work are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study's own results concern shallow ReLU regression, local parameter recovery and tensor versus random initialization. They do not test any listed version: width is fixed at K=5, and the initialization comparison does not examine activation matching or signal and gradient propagation.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors prove local linear convergence to the teacher parameters up to statistical error, assuming sufficiently close initialization, enough Gaussian-input samples and a bounded step size. Combining this with a cited tensor-initialization guarantee gives sample complexity linear in input dimension up to logarithmic factors, holding other problem parameters fixed. They leave theoretical guarantees for random initialization to future work.
record.recipe_differences: Synthetic teacher-student regression with Gaussian inputs and squared empirical loss; evaluates parameter recovery in a one-hidden-layer ReLU network rather than benchmark training classification error.
record.method_sensitivity: Tensor initialization converges faster early than random initialization in the reported synthetic experiment; both converge linearly after a number of iterations.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 6, Figure 2(a): with d=10, K=5, N=5000 and step size 0.5, both tensor and standard Gaussian initialization eventually yield linear convergence of empirical squared loss; tensor initialization converges faster early.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Tensor initialization can accelerate early training relative to random Gaussian initialization in this shallow teacher-student ReLU regression setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 6, Figure 2(b): noiseless recovery experiments with d=20, 50 and 100 use 10 trials per sample-size setting and a relative parameter-error threshold of 0.001. The authors interpret the curves against N/d as showing sample complexity linear in d.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Tensor initialization followed by gradient descent has sample complexity approximately linear in input dimension in the tested teacher-student setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 6, Figure 2(c): noisy experiments report average Frobenius parameter error over 10 trials for d=10, 25 and 50, with curves aligning against N/d. The theorem bounds squared Frobenius error at order d log N/N with other parameters fixed; the experiment reports the unsquared norm.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Recovery error depends on rescaled sample size in this noisy shallow ReLU setting; the plotted unsquared error alone does not establish the theorem's squared-error rate.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics
record.problems: Experiments use synthetic Gaussian inputs and a single shallow teacher-student setting with K=5. The convergence figure compares initialization methods but the text gives no numeric loss values or uncertainty. Sample-complexity and statistical-rate results are presented in plots, with 10 trials per setting; no benchmark classification tasks are evaluated.
record.rows_left_out: No rows: reported experimental outcomes concern synthetic regression parameter recovery, which none of the six claim versions names as its measured behavior. Figure 2(a–c), Section 6.

untested.parts: Training classification error in large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including random labels and model-size, stopping and regularization conditions.
Spurious-minimum frequencies as teacher and student widths grow, and the effect of adding student neurons.
Training degradation with depth and its prevention through identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Activation-matched initialization, preservation of signals and gradients, trainable depth, and orthogonal versus Gaussian weights or convolution kernels.
Training above the initial stability threshold, curvature dynamics, edge-of-stability behavior and divergence.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and normalization-free Fixup training.

record.verdict_notes: Change the reader's tests/T2 classification to discusses/T6. The empty rows are appropriate, and the excluded experimental results are already declared in rows_left_out. Figure 2(a) measures empirical loss, so describing every experiment solely as parameter recovery is inaccurate, but it still does not match V1's classification setting or V4's initialization mechanism.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR classification error, corrupted or random labels, and the stated large versus small model, stopping and regularization conditions.
Whether extra student width reduces spurious minima across teacher and student widths.
Depth, plain versus residual architectures, normalization and shortcut effects.
Activation-matched initialization, signal propagation, depth sweeps and orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization effects.
Learning rates above the stability limit, curvature dynamics and long-run loss behavior.
Batch normalization's effect on training speed, accuracy and learning-rate tolerance.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
